Open a Session on the server, subscribe to its Events, and read Intents
from the terminal. What the world says arrives as prose; what you type is
sent as typed, and the server parses it — this client decides nothing.

Lines starting with / are for the client, not the world:
  /protocol [on|off]   show the Intents sent and the Events received
  /help                list these
  /quit                leave (as does Ctrl-C, or Ctrl-D at an empty line)

A dropped connection is announced and retried with backoff; the stream
resumes from the last Event seen, and a resume the server cannot honor is
announced too — the transcript never silently skips. --output json writes
the raw Event stream to stdout, one envelope per line, and everything else
to stderr.

A stored credential is required: run `andara-cli auth login` first.

Usage:
  andara-cli play [flags]

Examples:
  andara-cli play
  > look
  > north
  > /protocol on
  > west
  ^C

  printf 'look\n' | andara-cli play --output json | jq .

Flags:
      --as string                 open the Session acting as this account ID (operator or game master; audited)
      --client-timeout duration   how long one Submit may wait for its answer (0 means --timeout)
  -h, --help                      help for play
      --no-history                do not read or write $XDG_STATE_HOME/andara/history
      --reconnect                 retry a dropped connection with backoff and resume the stream (default true)
      --show-protocol             start with protocol visibility on (/protocol toggles it)
      --world                     ask for World visibility: every Event, wherever it happens (game master or operator)

Global Flags:
      --config string           config file path (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/andara/cli.yaml)
      --credentials string      credential file path (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/andara/credentials.yaml)
      --log-level string        CLI diagnostic level (default "warn")
      --no-color                disable ANSI output
  -o, --output string           output format: human or json (default "human")
      --server-address string   server endpoint (gRPC/Connect over TLS) (default "localhost:8443")
      --timeout duration        per-command deadline (default 30s)
      --tls-ca string           CA bundle to trust (empty uses the system trust store)
